summary: Complete package upgrade restores a coherent Perl interpreter and native module set
changes: Upgraded eight packages together: Perl from the 5.42 series to 5.44, GraphicsMagick, Graphviz, ImageMagick, perl-clone, perl-html-parser, perl-xml-parser and Texinfo. Preserved all previous package archives and signatures for rollback. Updated repository metadata and generated package caches through standard hooks. Recorded private maintenance evidence and this sanitized receipt. No other installed package changed; monitored desktop, keyboard, repository, display-manager, GPU and security settings were preserved.
tests: ChatGPT OAuth valid. Package database consistency and detailed integrity checks on all eight packages passed before and after. All six external native Perl module package imports passed before and after; candidate interpreter and modules also imported successfully from isolated extraction before installation. Graphviz SVG generation, GraphicsMagick and ImageMagick PNG creation and identification, and Texinfo conversion passed. Final SVG parsing and expected Info text passed. Complete upgrade returned zero, with no hook errors or obsolete Perl module warnings. Fresh repository check returned no pending updates. No failed system units; monitored configuration hashes unchanged; SDDM enabled and existing timer policy preserved.
rollback: Exact previous archives, signatures, hashes and one complete pacman downgrade argument list retained privately for all eight packages. Rollback was not needed. Revalidate installed state before restoring the complete previous set with normal signature and dependency enforcement. No reboot or system-wide restoration was performed.
problem: A previously deferred update had selected native Perl modules for the 5.44 series while retaining an interpreter from the 5.42 series. Current configured repository metadata now supplies the interpreter and all installed native module package upgrades together. Some initial mirrors lacked old recovery archives; subsequent configured mirrors supplied them successfully.
solution: Validated the complete current candidate set with an isolated interpreter and module import check, preserved signed recovery archives, applied the full repository upgrade and verified installed functionality. Left a pre-existing locally newer libclc package unchanged; no repository reorder or pinning was introduced.
reproduction: Refresh isolated repository metadata and preview the complete transaction. Verify that the interpreter and every installed native Perl module package target the same Perl series. Download with normal signature checks, test candidate module imports from private extraction, then validate installed imports and Graphviz, image and Texinfo operations after the full transaction.
